sec: Severity classification, thirst threshold and ADH synthesis

items.q: Match the serum sodium concentration to its severity classification tier — 1) 130 to 135 mEq/L 2) 120 to 129 mEq/L 3) 100 to 119 mEq/L 4) Less than 100 mEq/L … A) Mild hyponatremia B) Moderate hyponatremia C) Severe hyponatremia D) Very severe hyponatremia
items.exp: 130-135 is mild, 120-129 is moderate, 100-119 is severe, and < 100 is very severe hyponatremia. (Book p959)

items.q: A 58-year-old female is admitted with a serum sodium of 114 mEq/L. On examination, she exhibits confusion, disorientation, wide-based gait abnormalities, and intractable hiccups. Her clinical severity tier is:
items.exp: Sodium of 100-119 mEq/L represents severe hyponatremia characterized by confusion, gait abnormalities, and hiccups. (Book p959)

items.q: What life-threatening clinical manifestations occur in very severe hyponatremia when serum sodium falls below 100 mEq/L?
opts: Features of increased intracranial tension and brain herniation
items.exp: Sodium < 100 mEq/L causes very severe hyponatremia with manifestations of increased intracranial tension (ICT). (Book p959)

items.q: Which obsolete laboratory methodology artifacts produce artifactual pseudohyponatremia due to volume displacement?
items.exp: Obsolete methodology causes of pseudohyponatremia are hypertriglyceridemia and paraproteinemia. (Book p959)

items.q: At what serum osmolality threshold is endogenous ADH (vasopressin) release triggered?
items.exp: ADH secretion is activated when serum osmolality exceeds 280 mmol/kg. (Book p959)

items.q: At what serum osmolality threshold is the physiological thirst mechanism activated?
items.exp: The thirst mechanism is activated when serum osmolality rises above 290 mmol/kg. (Book p959)

items.q: Assess the prevention of hypernatremia: I Hypernatremia is very rare because osmolality > 280 mmol/kg releases ADH and > 290 mmol/kg stimulates thirst. II Concomitant ADH-mediated water retention and thirst prevent hypernatremia under normal physiology.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Increased osmolality triggers ADH (> 280) and thirst (> 290), so elevated sodium is not normally seen. (Book p959)

items.q: Vasopressin is synthesized in the hypothalamus within the supra-optic and ___ nuclei.
items.exp: ADH is synthesized in the supra-optic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus. (Book p959)

items.q: What specialized hypothalamic neuronal cell population synthesizes pro-vasopressin?
items.exp: Magnocellular neurons produce the pro-vasopressin precursor. (Book p959)

items.q: Match the pro-vasopressin cleavage fragment to its role — 1) ADH (Vasopressin) 2) Neurophysin 3) Copeptin … A) Active antidiuretic hormone stored in posterior pituitary B) Carrier protein during axonal transport C) Equimolar C-terminal cleavage marker
items.exp: Pro-vasopressin is cleaved into ADH, neurophysin, and copeptin at the pituitary stalk. (Book p959)

items.q: Which stimulus is the MOST important physiological driver for ADH release?
items.exp: Osmotic stimulus (at 280 mOsm/kg) is the most important physiological trigger for ADH release. (Book p959)

items.q: Assess mild to moderate hyponatremia: I Sodium levels of 120 to 135 mEq/L cause gastrointestinal symptoms, mild headache, and lethargy. II Sodium levels between 120 and 135 mEq/L routinely cause seizures and tentorial herniation.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Mild to moderate hyponatremia (120-135) manifests with GI symptoms, mild headache, and lethargy, not herniation. (Book p959)
